documents.proposal:
# Fix multi-session Temporal read saturation

## Why

`adv_status` (all views, including lightweight `summary`) returns an unclassified `ToolExecutionTimeout` at the 10s host cap instead of bounded degraded data. This violates shipped spec law `rq-boundedAuthoritativeRead01`, which requires authoritative reads to return "a complete or explicitly degraded result — never an unclassified whole-tool ToolExecutionTimeout".

The failure reproduces under a healthy, unsaturated system (7 workers / 6 sessions, `adv_doctor` green, `adv_wip_state` fast), so it is not the multi-session saturation originally hypothesized. Saturation is an amplifier that shrinks margin.

Two structural gaps, both about how the 8s aggregate read budget is applied:

- **D1** — `adv_status` summary view passes no `deadline` in `StatusReadOptions`, so the store mints its own per-call deadline and the bootstrap retry loop can stack multiple fresh budgets.
- **D2** — where the budget *is* applied (`adv_change_show` enrichment), 8s sits too close to the 10s host cap: a single member can consume the entire aggregate, leaving under 2s for everything else.

Operators lose read access to change state during normal work, with no signal about which read failed or whether the data exists on disk.

## What Changes

- Supply a request-scoped deadline on the `adv_status` summary path, matching what the health view already does, so one budget governs the whole invocation rather than each store call.
- Make bootstrap retry admission honour the remaining request budget, so N attempts can never exceed one aggregate deadline.
- Reconsider `NOT_FOUND` retry admission: a missing workflow cannot become found by re-querying.
- Establish explicit headroom accounting between the aggregate read budget and the host tool cap, so degradation is always reached before the host kills execution.
- Add regression coverage asserting no read path can exceed the aggregate budget regardless of attempt count.

## User Outcomes

- [ ] `adv_status` returns usable data or an explicitly degraded result, never an opaque host timeout
- [ ] Degraded reads name what was unavailable and why, so the operator knows whether to retry, degrade, or investigate
- [ ] Read tools stay within the host cap under concurrent multi-session load
- [ ] No repair depends on restarting OpenCode or raising the host timeout cap
- [ ] Discovery will firm acceptance criteria and success criteria

## Affected Code

- `plugin/src/tools/status.ts` — summary path omits `deadline`; bootstrap retry loop does not honour a remaining budget
- `plugin/src/tools/status-health-plan.ts` — reference implementation; health view already supplies a deadline
- `plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/changes.ts` — per-call deadline minting when caller supplies none
- `plugin/src/temporal/retry-wrapper.ts` — aggregate budget constant and `NOT_FOUND` → `fallback` retry classification
- `plugin/src/tools/change.ts` — existing subread runner; headroom reference, already correctly bounded

## Constraints

- Must not raise the host tool-timeout cap or rely on an OpenCode restart as the durable repair.
- Must not add Temporal mutations or workflow signals to read paths.
- Must preserve disk-authoritative read behavior and existing typed degradation shipped by `fixChangeReadTimeouts`.
- Must keep health diagnostics global; no per-change workflow health probe.
- Must not regress genuine bootstrap-in-progress recovery, which the existing retry was written to serve.
- Degradation must stay typed and machine-checkable, not prose-inferred.

## Impact

Read-path behavior only; no schema or persistence format change, no migration. Callers that today receive a host timeout will instead receive a typed degraded payload — consumers treating any non-complete response as fatal must read the degradation marker.

## Risks

- Discovery has not yet instrumented where the 10s is actually spent. The retry-stacking mechanism is a structural worst-case bound, not a measured attribution; design must not commit before that is closed.
- Tightening `NOT_FOUND` retry admission could regress bootstrap-in-progress recovery. The two cases must be distinguished structurally, not heuristically.
- Lowering the aggregate budget for headroom trades completeness for bounded failure — it will degrade more often under load. That tradeoff needs explicit sign-off.
- Reproduction depends on ambient project state; regression tests must construct the unreachable-workflow condition deterministically.

## Validation Plan

- Instrument first: establish where `adv_status view:"summary"` spends its 10s before choosing a fix.
- Write failing tests (red): aggregate-budget enforcement across retry attempts; summary-path deadline propagation; `NOT_FOUND` retry admission; headroom between aggregate budget and host cap.
- Implement to green.
- Assert the negative explicitly: no read path exceeds the aggregate budget regardless of attempt count.
- Run full suite via `bin/oc-test` to verify no regression in disk-authoritative reads or existing typed degradation.
documents.problemStatement:
## Problem Statement

`adv_status` (all views, including lightweight `summary`) exceeds the 10s host SDK tool-execution cap and returns an unclassified `ToolExecutionTimeout` instead of a bounded degraded result.

This violates shipped spec law `rq-boundedAuthoritativeRead01` (`plugin/src/temporal/retry-wrapper.ts:197-203`): authoritative reads must "return a complete or explicitly degraded result — never an unclassified whole-tool ToolExecutionTimeout."

## Measured Evidence

Verified 2026-08-03 under a **healthy, unsaturated** system — 7 workers / 6 sessions, `adv_doctor` green on all four axes (`server_alive`, `worker_alive`, `queue_serviceable`, `search_attributes_ok`), `adv_wip_state` (a heavy read) returning fast:

- `adv_status view:"summary"` → `ToolExecutionTimeout` at 10000ms. Reproduced twice, ~25 minutes apart.
- `adv_change_show` bare → fast, `_source:"disk"`.
- `adv_task_list` / `adv_task_show` on an unreachable workflow → **fast**, typed `TemporalReadOutcomeError`. Correct bounded behavior.

A saturation-only hypothesis cannot explain a timeout under healthy, unsaturated conditions. Concurrency load is a contributing amplifier that shrinks margin, not the cause.

## Root Cause Analysis

**D1 — `adv_status` has no request-scoped deadline on the summary path.** Confirmed by direct source reading:

| Line | Fact |
|---|---|
| `plugin/src/tools/status.ts:345-350` | `view === "summary"` builds `{ recentLimit }` — **no `deadline` field** |
| `plugin/src/storage/store-types.ts:134-136` | Documented contract: "`deadline` lets a caller share one request-scoped aggregate deadline across the status read. **Stores create their own per-call deadline when it is absent.**" |
| `plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/changes.ts:808` | Store consequently mints its own fresh 8s deadline per call |
| `plugin/src/tools/status.ts:148-170` | `loadStatusWithBootstrapRetry` loops up to `STATUS_BOOTSTRAP_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3`, retrying whenever `classifyTemporalError(error) === "fallback"` |
| `plugin/src/temporal/retry-wrapper.ts:172-179` | `NOT_FOUND` is classified `fallback` — i.e. retry-admitted, though a missing workflow cannot become found by re-querying |
| `plugin/src/tools/status-health-plan.ts:802-816` | The `health` view **does** supply a deadline — summary was simply missed |

**Attribution honesty:** the resulting "up to 3 × 8s" is a structural **worst-case upper bound, not a measured value**. The retry fires only when `store.status()` *throws*; a degraded return does not retry. What is measured is the >10s summary timeout under healthy conditions. Discovery must instrument where the 10s is actually spent before design commits to a mechanism.

**D2 — enrichment aggregate budget leaves insufficient margin under the host cap.** Originally filed as "enrichment has no deadline"; that was **wrong and is retracted**. `adv_change_show` enrichment *is* bounded via `createTemporalReadContext` (`plugin/src/tools/change.ts:1510`) and `createChangeShowSubreadRunner` (`change.ts:172-189`), giving a shared 8s aggregate plus a hardcoded 1500ms per-member cap, `maxAttempts: 1`, with typed degradation through `hydrationStats`. Verified working:

```
_readyTasksError:      "Temporal operation exceeded 507ms timeout"
_contextSnapshotError: "Temporal operation exceeded 1500ms timeout"
_artifactsError:       "Temporal operation exceeded 8000ms timeout"
hydrationStats: { deadlineExceeded: true, omitted: 3,
                  omittedIds: ["snapshot","readyTasks","artifacts"] }
```

The real defect is margin: `_artifactsError` shows a **single member consuming the entire 8s aggregate**, leaving under 2s beneath the 10s host cap for base change load plus remaining members. Under load this still exceeds the cap — which is what was observed at session start, when the same call returned `ToolExecutionTimeout`. The 8s budget was chosen without explicit headroom accounting against the 10s host cap.

**Unifying theme:** the 8s aggregate budget is applied inconsistently (absent on `adv_status` summary, present on `adv_change_show`) and, where present, is set too close to the 10s host cap to guarantee degradation is reached before the host kills execution.

## User Impact

`adv_status` intermittently returns no usable data during normal work. The failure is opaque: an unclassified host timeout gives no signal about which underlying read failed or whether the data exists on disk, and its stock hint recommends an OpenCode restart that does not address the cause.

## Out of scope

- Raising the host tool-timeout cap, or an OpenCode restart, as the durable repair.
- The archived `fixHealthViewTimeouts` health execution budget — correct for its scoped problem, not a cause here.
- Per-session worker spawn admission control, orphan session-queue reclamation (40+ tracked, 0 adopted), and worker memory footprint (1.3–2.7 GB RSS each). Real load-side contributors that shrink margin, but a separate change.
- Killing active user work sessions; acute relief stays user-initiated.

## Related

- `rq-boundedAuthoritativeRead01` / `rq-boundedAuthoritativeRead03` — governing spec law.

# Agreement

## Objectives

1. Guarantee that authoritative ADV read tools always return a complete or explicitly degraded result within the host tool-execution cap, never an unclassified `ToolExecutionTimeout`.
2. Apply the request-scoped read deadline uniformly across every `adv_status` view, not just `health`.
3. Make the relationship between the aggregate read budget and the host tool cap structural and machine-checked rather than two independently-chosen constants.

## Success Criteria

1. `adv_status` returns usable or explicitly-degraded data under concurrent multi-session load without operator intervention.
2. An operator seeing a degraded read can tell what was unavailable and why, without inspecting logs or restarting OpenCode.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given any `adv_status` view (`summary`, `health`, `changes`, `hygiene`), when the read runs, then it executes under a single request-scoped aggregate deadline supplied by the caller. [warrant: tool:adv_status]
2. Given a store read that exhausts the aggregate budget, when `adv_status` responds, then it returns typed degraded output identifying the unavailable source, and never an unclassified whole-tool `ToolExecutionTimeout`. [warrant: tool:adv_status]
3. Given the bootstrap retry loop, when it makes N attempts, then total elapsed time across all attempts remains within the one request-scoped aggregate deadline; no attempt mints a fresh budget.
4. Given a `NOT_FOUND` classification for an unreachable workflow, when retry admission is evaluated, then the read does not re-attempt the same query, and genuine bootstrap-in-progress recovery remains functional and distinguishable structurally rather than heuristically.
5. Given the aggregate read budget and the host tool-execution cap, when either constant changes, then a machine-checked relationship enforces sufficient headroom for degradation to be reached and serialized before the host cap fires.
6. Evidence: per-view deadline propagation, aggregate-budget enforcement across retry attempts, `NOT_FOUND` retry admission, bootstrap-recovery preservation, and the budget-to-cap headroom invariant are verified via automated regression tests.

## Constraints

1. Must not raise the host tool-timeout cap, globally or per-tool, as the means of satisfying the criteria.
2. Must not rely on an OpenCode restart, worker restart, or session termination as the durable repair.
3. Must not add Temporal mutations or workflow signals to read paths.
4. Must preserve disk-authoritative read behavior and existing typed degradation shipped by `fixChangeReadTimeouts`.
5. Must keep health diagnostics global; no per-change workflow health probe.
6. Must not regress genuine bootstrap-in-progress recovery.
7. Degradation must be typed and machine-checkable, never prose-inferred.

## Avoidances

1. Do not treat concurrency saturation as the root cause; it is an amplifier.
2. Do not lower the aggregate budget as an unexamined blanket fix — the completeness-versus-bounded-failure tradeoff requires explicit design justification.
3. Do not introduce a second parallel deadline mechanism; extend the existing `TemporalReadContext`.
4. Do not expand scope into worker admission control, orphan-queue reclamation, or worker memory footprint.

## Preview Applicability

preview_expectation: exact_route_required: not_applicable; data_state_expectation: not_applicable; viewport_expectation: not_applicable.
Rationale: internal read-path and tool-timeout behavior has no browser-visible surface.

## Decisions

### User Decisions

- Fold the read-path defects into this change rather than opening a fifth sibling change on the same surface.
- Accept the corrected RCA and leave the proposal gate complete; the RCA Revision Note preserves the audit trail.
- Design from established structural evidence now rather than pausing discovery to instrument runtime attribution first.

### Agent Decisions (LBP)

- Treat the `health` view's existing `buildHealthStatusReadOptions` as the reference implementation and extend that pattern to the remaining three views, rather than inventing a new mechanism.
- Bind the aggregate read budget to the host tool cap structurally, so headroom cannot silently erode when either constant is edited independently.
- Prefer removing `NOT_FOUND` from retry admission over shortening the retry loop, since re-querying a missing workflow cannot succeed and consumes budget that degradation needs.

## Open Risk Accepted At Sign-Off

Runtime attribution for the observed 10s `adv_status` timeout was not instrumented before design. The structural gaps are established by direct source reading, but the precise time distribution within the failing call is unmeasured. Implementation tests must confirm the fix actually eliminates the observed timeout, not merely satisfy the structural criteria — if they do not, the change re-enters discovery rather than proceeding.

# Design

## Causal Model — validated

| View | Path | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| `summary`, `changes`, `hygiene` | non-`sourceRanked` (`index.ts:1777`) | **D6** — unconditional archive corpus load |
| `health` | `sourceRanked` (`index.ts:1706-1772`) | **D4a** — unbounded pre-ranking diskId enumeration |

Validator confirmed the branch split in production: `status.ts:348-349` → `buildHealthStatusReadOptions` (`sourceRanked: true`) → `index.ts:1700` bounded branch. Summary/changes/hygiene pass no `sourceRanked` (`status.ts:345-350`) and fall through to `changeOps.listSummary` (`index.ts:1777`).

## THE THREE IMPLEMENTATION SITES

Planning must enumerate all three explicitly. Scoping from a one-line summary of D6 will produce a change that passes the host-cap fixture while leaving a residual production breach path under corpus pressure.

### Site 1 — unconditional archive load (`changes.ts:888-901`)  **[dominant cost, 3 views]**
The archive `loadChange` loop runs unconditionally inside `if (legacy.paths.archive)` — **526 JSON parses on pokeedge, 484+ here — whether or not `wantsTerminalStatuses`**. The loaded data is only *used* at `:917` when terminal statuses are wanted; the I/O is paid regardless. This, not the summary shard read, is the dominant cost inside `listSummary`.

Fix: skip the loop entirely when terminal statuses are not requested; add per-iteration admission when it does run. `rq-readSourceAttribution01.2` (`spec.json:1779-1790`) requires per-iteration admission in the archive-inventory × candidate scan; current code relies on throw-on-expiry via `raceWithTemporalDeadline`, not a pre-iteration gate — currently unmet.

### Site 2 — per-call deadline replacement (`changes.ts:808`)
**Correction to earlier framing:** `readProjectionChangeList` (`changes.ts:793`) *does* create a deadline — its **own** 8s one at `:808`. The defect is that it is per-call rather than threaded from the caller's request budget, so it cannot compose with the aggregate. Replace with the caller-supplied context; mint locally only as fallback.

### Site 3 — health pre-ranking enumeration (`index.ts:1098-1133`)
`mapWithConcurrency(diskIds, 4, …)` reads `change.json` for **every** diskId before `candidateLimit` is applied at `:1144`. Each iteration checks `expired()` (`:1102`) so it is deadline-gated, but it sits outside the 7.5s plan budget D4 enforces. This is where health's time goes — the design's original "headroom" explanation was incomplete.

The A.1/A.2 harness (`status-health-integration-blockers.test.ts:620-664`) seeds 20 disk candidates and mocks `listSourceRankedCandidates`. Production performs hundreds of real disk reads the harness never exercises. **That is why those tests pass while production breaches** — the reproduction test must not repeat this omission.

## Measured Evidence

| Observation | Consequence |
|---|---|
| All four views exceed the 10s cap (4 reproductions) | Two mechanisms, not one |
| `health` breaches despite bounded plan + green tests (9/9) | Falsified enrichment loop as cause; led to Site 3 |
| `adv_spec list` instant | Falsified `listSpecsFilesystem` (`index.ts:1692`) |
| `target_path` disk-snapshot fast at greater scale (pokeedge: 212 changes, 526 archives) | Cost is Temporal-path only |
| `adv_change_list` fast on same corpus | It bounds; `buildTemporalStatus` does not |
| `adv_doctor` green at failure, 7 workers / 6 sessions | Not saturation |

## D6 — Bound the status corpus fetch  **[primary causal fix, 3 views]**

Covers Sites 1 and 2.

1. Skip the archive load loop when terminal statuses are not requested (Site 1).
2. Add per-iteration admission when it does run (Site 1, `rq-readSourceAttribution01.2`).
3. Thread the caller's request deadline into `listSummary`/`readProjectionChangeList` instead of per-call minting (Site 2).
4. Apply the candidate bound at fetch time, not post-slice — filtering/slicing currently happens after the fetch at `index.ts:1794-1820`.
5. Source `byStatus` counts from summary shards. **Validator confirmed feasible**: `summary.status` is present per row (`changes.ts:591-592`). If a chosen approach cannot produce exact counts within budget, return typed degraded counts — never an unbounded fetch.
6. Typed degradation consistent with the existing `SOURCE_BOUND_EXCEEDED` shape (`index.ts:1826-1839`).

**Amplifier, not scope.** The in-flight filter admits terminal-status changes (~25 of 49; corroborated — `fixChangeReadTimeouts`, `fixHealthFieldScope` both listed `draft`, both `archived`). Inflates Site 1 further. Separate change; see wisdom `ws-q3iBV2`.

## D4 — Headroom, and D4a — bound health pre-ranking  **[causal for health]**

**D4a (Site 3).** Bring the pre-ranking diskId enumeration under the request budget, or apply `candidateLimit` before enumeration rather than after. Deadline-gating per iteration is insufficient — the work must be bounded, not merely interruptible.

**D4 (headroom).** Derive `READ_DEADLINE_BUDGET = DEFAULT_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS - TOOL_RESPONSE_HEADROOM_MS` with a CI-enforced invariant (AC5). Constant is consumed by `change.ts`, `epic.ts`, `status-health.ts`, `status-execution.ts`; `adv_status` runs on the 10s default (`tool-registry.ts:784`), `adv_change_archive` overrides to 600s (`tool-registry.ts:1135`). State explicitly whether the change is global or status-local; if global, the invariant must hold for every consumer. Reserve value must be measured, not guessed.

**Tradeoff (Avoidance 2).** Larger reserve → smaller budget → more frequent degradation. Accepted: bounded typed failure beats opaque timeout.

## D1 — Request-scoped deadline for every view

Create one `TemporalReadContext` in the handler before `loadStatusWithBootstrapRetry`; thread into `StatusReadOptions` for all views; `buildHealthStatusReadOptions` receives it rather than constructing its own.

**AMENDMENT.** Threading into `StatusReadOptions` alone is insufficient — the deadline must reach Sites 1, 2, and 3. Verify by tracing each call, not by assuming the option is honoured.

## D2 — Retry admission against remaining budget

Admission-check the shared context before each attempt in `loadStatusWithBootstrapRetry` (`status.ts:148-170`); return typed degraded output on expiry. Caveat: "3 × 8s" is a structural worst case, never observed. Not a causal claim.

## D3 — Bootstrap-in-progress vs permanently-absent

Do not touch shared `classifyTemporalError` (`retry-wrapper.ts:145-181`). Narrow admission at the `status.ts` call site: retry admitted when no durable disk projection exists; refused when one exists. **Soundness verified at source** — `dualWriteAfterMutation` (`index.ts:383-395`) returns early unless outcome `confirmed` and `readbackValue` present.

Required: regression test asserting no path writes a projection without prior confirmed readback; distinguish `NOT_FOUND` from `TMPRL1100` (`retry-wrapper.ts:152-156`); projection check reads already-loaded disk state only.

## D5 — Bound the post-status enrichment loop

`status.ts:424-476` cutoff guard at `:429-431` is health-only; the `else` branch at `:458-473` loops candidates unbounded. Same at `:481`, `:550`, `:810`, `:836`, `:845`. Fix: admission check per candidate, per-member cap via `runTemporalRead(..., { maxAttempts: 1 })` mirroring `change.ts:186`, typed omissions via `hydrationStats` (`change.ts:209-216`).

**Not causal** — falsified by measurement. Retained as a real unbounded-work defect closing the `rq-boundedAuthoritativeRead01` candidate-hydration obligation.

**Campsite.** `status-health-integration-blockers.test.ts` header claims blockers A/B/C unfixed; they pass 9/9. Correct the stale comments.

## Spec Conformance

- `rq-boundedAuthoritativeRead01` (`spec.json:1697`) — summary/changes/hygiene currently **violate** it (no deadline, `status.ts:345-350`). D1+D6 corrective.
- `rq-readSourceAttribution01.2` (`spec.json:1779-1790`) — per-iteration admission in the archive scan currently **unmet** (`changes.ts:888-901`). D6 Site 1 corrective.
- `rq-summaryReadBound01` (`spec.json:1796`) — demands the bound apply in the shared resolver via `listResolvedChanges` `candidateLimit`. Summary does not use that resolver; the claim at `status.ts:337-344` describes **unmet intent**. D6 satisfies the intent via a different mechanism. Resolve the comment-vs-code divergence explicitly.

No spec-law conflict. All three are corrective, not contradictory.

## Verification Strategy — binding

1. **Reproduction preserved:** `plugin/src/tools/status-host-cap.test.ts`, four views failing `expect(parsed.errorClass).not.toBe("ToolExecutionTimeout")`, run `tr_msdv6zd5_470ce7e6`.
2. **Fixture must exercise corpus pressure.** The existing health harness seeds only 20 disk candidates and mocks the ranking call — that is precisely why it passes while production breaches. The reproduction must include a realistic archive corpus.
3. **Prove elimination, not conformance.** AC1–AC5 passing is insufficient; RED → GREEN required.
4. **Re-measure the live symptom** on all four views after deploy.
5. **If the symptom survives**, re-enter rather than ship. Do not weaken the test.

## Validator Dispositions

Pass 1: CONFLICT, five findings, all accepted (F2 → D5; F4 accepted with evidence replaced; F1 → D3 invariant test; F3 → D4 scope; F5 → threading obligation).

Pass 2: CAUTION. Findings 1/3/6 confirm the model, count feasibility, and absence of spec conflict. Findings 2/4/5 corrected the design: health's cost is Site 3 not headroom alone; `listSummary` does have a deadline (per-call, `changes.ts:808`) and the dominant cost is the unconditional archive loop (Site 1); `rq-summaryReadBound01` is unmet. Additional risk accepted: implementation scoped from D6's one-line summary would under-reach — hence the explicit three-site enumeration above.

## Out of Scope

Working-set correctness (separate change), worker admission control, orphan session-queue reclamation, worker memory footprint, host tool cap changes.

# Executive Summary

## Outcome
The project status command (`adv_status`) currently hangs and fails with an unexplained timeout instead of returning an answer. This change makes it always return either a complete result or a clearly-labelled partial result within its time limit. You are approving the fix to move to release preparation.

## Why It Matters
`adv_status` is the primary way an operator or agent checks the state of a project. Today it can fail with no usable information, and a previous attempt at this fix was shipped and deployed but the failure continued — so this work carries direct evidence that the remaining cause was found and closed. When the system is under pressure, users now get a partial answer that names what was unavailable, rather than a dead end that requires restarting the tool.

## Verdict
APPROVED

## What Was Built
1. **Bounded the slow step that survived the last attempt** (D5) — after the main data load finished, a follow-up step that enriched each change ran with no time limit, which is why the earlier deploy did not fix the problem. It is now time-limited, along with every other post-load step (per-iteration deadline admission in both enrichment branches; `cutoffAt`/`signal` threaded into `enrichRecentChangeStatus`).
2. **Stopped pointless retries against a permanently-missing record** (D3) — the system used to retry a lookup that could never succeed, burning the time budget needed to produce a useful answer. It now tells the difference structurally, using a numeric error code plus request-scoped state rather than by pattern-matching error text.
3. **Tied the internal time budget to the external time limit** (D4) — these were two independent numbers that could drift apart silently. The budget is now calculated from the limit, with the safety reserve measured (199 ms, from a 132 ms worst case over 100 runs of a large payload) rather than guessed, and a CI check that fails if the relationship is ever broken.
4. **Verification and re-entry decision** — confirmed every identified unbounded path is now bounded across the data, tool, retry, and configuration layers.

## What Was Verified
- Verdict: APPROVED with 14 findings (2 blockers, 4 issues, 7 suggestions, 1 nit); all blockers and issues fixed, 2 suggestions rejected with evidence
- Tests: 11-file targeted sweep passing (`tr_mseuouaq_138a5344`); `pnpm run check` clean, 0 errors (`tr_mseuredd_ed4d7913`)

Bounded the post-load enrichment step that ran with no time limit — the cause that survived the previous deploy of this fix
Stopped futile retries against a permanently-missing workflow, using a structural error code plus request-scoped state rather than error-text matching
The internal read budget is now derived from the host tool cap with a measured safety reserve and a CI-enforced invariant, so the two can no longer drift apart silently

Remediated in 76f943d9 with a request-scoped DiskProjectionReadState; RED-verified ('expected 2 to be 4') then GREEN. Bootstrap recovery and TMPRL1100 retry now covered by explicit tests.

Saturation is not treated as root cause. The fix bounds aggregate reads at the store, tool, retry, and constant layers; the change title remains stale but the implemented causal model is the unbounded-read model established in design.

The budget was not lowered as a blanket fix — it was RAISED from the accidental 8000ms default to a derived 9801ms, with the 199ms reserve measured rather than guessed and the completeness/degradation tradeoff documented in tool-budgets.ts.

No second parallel deadline mechanism. STATUS_READ_DEADLINE_BUDGET_MS is a derived budget VALUE fed into the existing createTemporalReadContext / TemporalReadContext; TEMPORAL_READ_DEADLINE_BUDGET_MS remains only the default for callers that supply no budget.

Scope confined to status read bounding, projection marking, NOT_FOUND admission, budget constants, and tests. No worker admission control, orphan-queue reclamation, or worker memory work. Contract-traceability scan reported zero out-of-scope changes.
